metadata.audience: High school students + parents planning service hours
metadata.purpose: Insider volunteer insights — what AOs actually look for, hidden leadership pathways, scholarship-linked service, in-state vs national org access, the 'sustained vs sporadic' nuance.

sections.title: What admissions officers actually look for in service

items.label: Sustained > sporadic, by a lot
items.detail: AOs at HYPSM-tier schools have repeatedly published that 200 hours at one organization beats 200 hours across 5 organizations. Demonstrates commitment, growth, and depth of impact. Pick one or two and stay 3-4 years.

items.label: Leadership growth beats hour count
items.detail: Moving from volunteer → committee member → coordinator → board liaison over 4 years tells a story. 500 hours of unchanged volunteer role tells a different story. Story matters more than count.

items.label: Don't pad the activity list
items.detail: Common App allows 10 activities. AOs see padded lists and discount the depth of every entry. Better to list 5 substantive activities than 10 light ones.

items.label: CIT pipeline at major camps
items.detail: YMCA, Camp Fire, BGCA all have Counselor-In-Training programs for ages 13-15. Free or discounted attendance + leadership training. Apply year before turning 14. Often leads to paid junior counselor role at 16-17 — a strong work + leadership signal.

items.label: Hospital 'Junior Volunteer Leadership Council'
items.detail: Most major hospitals' Junior Volunteer programs have an internal leadership track — student board, peer mentor program, etc. Self-nominate after 6 months as regular volunteer. Way fewer applicants than the regular junior volunteer pool.

items.label: Local nonprofit board student seat
items.detail: Many small-to-mid nonprofits have a 'student member' seat on their board, often unfilled. Email the executive director directly with a brief proposal. Boards under 15 members often welcome the youth perspective.

items.label: Bonner Scholars Program
items.detail: 60+ colleges offer the Bonner Scholarship — full or partial tuition in exchange for service commitment during college. Apply during senior-year college applications. Demonstrates pre-college service commitment is the eligibility differentiator.

items.label: Coca-Cola Scholars Foundation
items.detail: 150 students/year, $20K each. Service is one of three pillars (leadership + academics + service). Application opens August of senior year. Sustained multi-year service is the differentiator vs episodic.

items.label: AmeriCorps Education Award
items.detail: Year-long full-time service after HS = ~$7K toward college. Stack with Pell Grant + state aid. City Year (year-long teaching support) is the highest-prestige program in the network.

sections.title: What NOT to do (voluntourism + checkbox traps)

items.label: International 'mission trip' service is heavily discounted by AOs
items.detail: Two weeks building a school in another country reads as expensive tourism. AOs explicitly devalue these unless the family has a sustained connection to the community. If you must do international service, do it through year-round partnership orgs that serve via virtual mentorship + occasional in-person visits, not 1-2 week trips.

items.label: 'Service hour' graduation requirements don't impress
items.detail: Most HS districts require 40-100 service hours to graduate. Meeting this minimum is invisible. Doubling it without a clear story is also invisible. Triple it AND have growth + impact and now you have something.

items.label: Avoid 'starting your own nonprofit' unless you really mean it
items.detail: AOs have seen 50,000 student-founded nonprofits. The ones that move the needle have real 501(c)(3) status, sustained 3+ year operating history, audited finances, and measurable impact. Most student nonprofits don't meet this bar — and AOs can tell from the application.

sections.title: From the field — fresh insider notes (auto-discovered)

items.sourceName: Greentrike / Children's Museum of Tacoma Volunteer
items.insight: TEEN ONBOARDING IS A 4-6 WEEK PIPELINE, NOT A WALK-IN. Required order: (1) submit Volunteer Contact + Application Form on greentrike.org/about/volunteer; (2) wait for a volunteer lead to email you the handbook and (for 14-17 yr olds) the parent/guardian permission form — the form is NOT downloadable upfront, so don't try to grab it; (3) attend an Interview & Orientation meeting; (4) clear background check + COVID-19 prevention protocols; (5) THEN sign up for a shift. If your teen wants to be a Program Assistant for summer camps or Play to Learn (shifts: half-hour before + after each program), apply by mid-May at the latest to clear the pipeline before camp season. Specific contact: Jen McDonald, jmcdonald@greentrike.org.

items.sourceName: Greentrike / Children's Museum of Tacoma Volunteer
items.insight: JBLM SITE = ENTIRELY SEPARATE TRACK. The Children's Museum at JBLM (2275 Liggett Ave, Joint Base Lewis-McChord) requires volunteers to ALSO register with the military's VMIS system at myarmyonesource.com — separate registration on top of Greentrike's Volunteer Contact Form. Plan: if your family is not military-connected and doesn't already have base access, choose the Tacoma site (1501 Pacific Ave, Suite 202) instead to skip VMIS entirely. The two sites share volunteer roles but onboarding paths do NOT cross-credit.

items.sourceName: Greentrike / Children's Museum of Tacoma Volunteer
items.insight: SKILLS-BUILD INTERN ROLE FOR HS/COLLEGE STUDENTS — the Communications & Marketing Volunteer Intern position is explicitly aimed at students focused on graphic design, copywriting, marketing, or communications. Output is real portfolio material (museum-event collateral, county-wide program graphics) — distinct from generic floor-volunteer hours. Apply via the same Volunteer Contact Form but specify role interest in the comment field; Jen McDonald (jmcdonald@greentrike.org) confirms current openings. Strong fit for a teen building a creative/marketing-focused college app.

items.sourceName: Mobius Discovery Center Volunteer (Spokane)
items.insight: CENTER IS TEMPORARILY CLOSED + VOLUNTEER APPLICATIONS PAUSED (as of April 2026). The mobiusdiscoverycenter.org site banner reads 'Temporarily Closed' and the volunteer page explicitly states 'Our next round of volunteer opportunities will open in November.' If you submit the Volunteer Application now, you'll be queued and contacted in November. Eastern WA families wanting Spokane-area youth-museum volunteer hours BEFORE November should pivot to Spark Central, Spokane Public Library teen advisory boards, or Riverfront Park event volunteering instead.

items.sourceName: Mobius Discovery Center Volunteer (Spokane)
items.insight: AGE FLOOR HAS A YOUNGER-SIBLING LOOPHOLE that's atypical for WA museums. Headline minimum is 16, BUT children 15 and under may volunteer if accompanied by an adult 18+. This is more permissive than the broader WA museum-cluster default (most require 14+ to volunteer alone, no parent-accompaniment path). Useful for parent + younger-sibling team service projects, especially since shifts include simple art-supply prep (e.g., punching paper flowers) that's age-appropriate for elementary-age helpers paired with a parent.

items.sourceName: Mobius Discovery Center Volunteer (Spokane)
items.insight: OFFSITE SHIFT PATH AT ELEMENTARY SCHOOLS — Mobius shifts may occur at the museum (331 N Post St, downtown Spokane) AND/OR at elementary schools across the Spokane area for outreach programming. If you're outside walking distance of downtown but live near a Spokane Public Schools site, ask Volunteer Manager Alina Morrisey (amorrisey@mobiusspokane.org) which schools host outreach shifts — can save a 20-30 min commute. Especially relevant for north-Spokane and Spokane Valley families.

items.sourceName: The Sophia Way Volunteer (Bellevue / Eastside Women's Shelters)
items.insight: DEDICATED HS LEADERSHIP TRACK = YOUTH ENGAGEMENT COMMITTEE. This is an explicit pathway for high schoolers to take ownership of donation drives, Community Brunches, and fundraising events — NOT just floor-volunteer hours. Meets the 4th Monday of every month online from 6-7pm, so it works around school + sports + commute (no Bellevue/Kirkland transport needed for the meeting itself). Strong college-app material: leadership of measurable outcomes (donation drives, fundraising results) with a documented monthly cadence. Apply via volunteer@sophiaway.org.

items.sourceName: The Sophia Way Volunteer (Bellevue / Eastside Women's Shelters)
items.insight: SHELTER-ASSISTANT ROLE HAS THREE GATES, NOT JUST AN AGE FLOOR: (a) volunteers must IDENTIFY AS WOMEN (this is a women's shelter, kitchen-area role); (b) 18+ to serve alone, ages 13-17 with parent/guardian; (c) HIDDEN COST — a current Washington food worker card is REQUIRED before any kitchen shift (~$10, foodworkercard.wa.gov, online course ~1 hour, valid 2-3 years). Get the card BEFORE signing up to avoid being turned away day-of. Lunch shifts: 10am-1pm; dinner shifts: 5:45pm-8pm. Two locations: Sophia's Place (Bellevue) + Helen's Place (Kirkland).

items.sourceName: The Sophia Way Volunteer (Bellevue / Eastside Women's Shelters)
items.insight: REMOTE-FROM-HOME PATH FOR FAMILIES WHO CAN'T COMMIT TO ONSITE SHIFTS — 'Prepare a Hot Meal' is fully offsite, can be one-time or recurring, and meals can be delivered HOT or FROZEN (frozen drop-off means you don't have to time delivery to a meal-service window). Tagged on the site as 'one of our greatest needs.' Capacity per dropoff: Sophia's Place serves lunch for 30 / dinner for 21 daily; Helen's Place serves lunch + dinner for 40 daily. Great fit for a family with younger kids who can cook together but can't commit to a recurring shelter shift. No physical requirements, no food worker card required for cook-and-deliver (only for in-shelter kitchen).

items.sourceName: Treehouse for Kids — Volunteer & Treehouse Store
items.insight: ONGOING ROLES ARE AT CAPACITY (as of April 2026). The official volunteer page openly states: 'We are currently at capacity for all ongoing roles in the Treehouse Store, so we are not onboarding additional volunteers at this time.' If your teen wants to start NOW: skip the ongoing-role waitlist and book a one-time individual shift via the Treehouse Store calendar (labeled 'Holiday Helper', 'Individuals', 'Families', 'Friends', or 'Treehouse Admin Support'). Email volunteer@treehouseforkids.org to be added to the ongoing-role waitlist for whenever capacity reopens.

items.sourceName: Treehouse for Kids — Volunteer & Treehouse Store
items.insight: AGE FLOORS VARY BY SHIFT TYPE — read each calendar listing. (1) Group shifts: 12+, with a 5:1 student-to-adult ratio for middle schoolers; under 18 needs a guardian-signed waiver. (2) One-time individual shifts: 10+, 12+, or 16+ depending on the SPECIFIC shift (some allow a 10-year-old with parent, others 12+, others 16+); under 16 needs 1:1 adult chaperone. (3) Ongoing roles: 12+ (with adult) or 16+ (alone). Tell parents: don't assume the 12+ floor — check the exact shift's calendar listing.

items.sourceName: Treehouse for Kids — Volunteer & Treehouse Store
items.insight: GROUP SHIFTS = GREAT FIT FOR YOUTH-GROUP / SCOUT / SERVICE-CLUB ONE-DAY PROJECTS. Capacity 5-15 volunteers, mostly Tue-Sat 10am-4pm at the Treehouse Store (2100 24th Ave S, Seattle 98144). Limited evenings. Email volunteer@treehouseforkids.org with desired date range; scheduling is flexible week-to-week. Tasks: sort/process incoming donations, fulfill online orders, tag clothing, prep store for shopping days. Useful when a service-hour deadline is approaching and ongoing roles are full.

items.sourceName: Second Harvest Inland Northwest Volunteer (Sort, Pack, Teaching Kitchen)
items.insight: AGE POLICY IS STRICTER THAN IT SOUNDS: minors UNDER 14 must stay WITH the parent/chaperone IN THE ASSIGNED WORK AREA — they cannot wander to other stations or work alongside peer volunteers. NO children under 9, period. Practical impact: a 10-year-old + parent get assigned together as a parent-child team, not as parallel independent workers. Teen-only sign-up starts at 14. For some events the minimum age is even higher — always check the event description on the calendar before driving over.

items.sourceName: Second Harvest Inland Northwest Volunteer (Sort, Pack, Teaching Kitchen)
items.insight: TWO FACILITIES, THREE PHONE LINES — call the right one. Spokane Volunteer Center: (509) 252-6252 for sort/pack shifts and food-drive driver program (no commercial license needed). The Kitchen (Spokane teaching-kitchen program for hands-on cooking): separate (509) 534-6678 line. Tri-Cities (Pasco) facility uses a different intake. Calling the wrong number is the #1 reason families say 'they never got back to me.' Drivers + Kitchen are distinct programs with their own onboarding — useful for teens with a culinary interest (Kitchen) or a license + truck (food-drive driver).

items.sourceName: Reading Partners
items.insight: 2025-26 SCHOOL-YEAR RECRUITMENT IS CLOSED (as of late April 2026). Reading Partners is now accepting applications for the 2026-27 school year (sessions begin around September). High-school students hoping to start hours in May/June need to either commit to fall 2026 OR pivot to a different literacy-tutoring program for spring/summer hours. Apply NOW for fall — earliest applicants typically get the most flexible school placements.

items.sourceName: Reading Partners
items.insight: TUTORING WINDOW IS AFTER-SCHOOL, IN-PERSON, AT TITLE 1 ELEMENTARIES. Sessions run Mon-Fri 2:30-4:00pm (some midday 12:00-3:00 slots), each tutor commits ~1 hour/week minimum, and you must reside in the Puget Sound region. Practical implications: (a) high-school students need an early-release day or AP-light schedule; (b) homeschoolers can use the noon slot; (c) college students with 2pm class blocks can't fit; (d) add 30-60 min round-trip drive/transit time to the partner elementary. Required: pass a background check + complete tutor orientation BEFORE first session. Curriculum and ongoing coaching provided.

items.sourceName: Reading Partners
items.insight: WA FOOTPRINT IS PUGET SOUND ONLY. Reading Partners' Wayfinder entry lists WA among 10+ states, but the WA presence is exclusively Puget Sound K-4 elementary schools. Spokane, Tri-Cities, Vancouver, Yakima, and Bellingham families need a different literacy-tutoring channel — try Communities In Schools chapters, local public-library tutor-volunteer programs, or Boys & Girls Club homework-help shifts. Don't assume statewide coverage from the entry.

items.sourceName: FareStart Volunteer (Kitchen, Events, Job-Skills Support)
items.insight: FareStart actually runs THREE distinct volunteer tracks — Community & School Meals (kitchen prep + meal-pack for school nutrition partners), Event Staffing & Administration (galas, fundraisers, Guest Chef Night, office tasks), and Food Resourcing & Distribution (gleaning fresh produce from partner farms + outdoor distribution to underserved neighborhoods). Pick by your teen's skill match: kitchen-curious → Community Meals; social/extroverted → Event Staffing; outdoor/logistics-minded → Food Resourcing. Wayfinder's current description collapses these into 'kitchen support' which under-sells the Food Resourcing farm-to-table track that develops genuine supply-chain operations skill.

items.sourceName: FareStart Volunteer (Kitchen, Events, Job-Skills Support)
items.insight: Capacity reality check from FareStart's own 2023 stats: 640 volunteers logged 5,778 hours across 1,447 individual shifts — averaging only ~9 hours / 2.3 shifts per volunteer per year. FareStart treats volunteers as occasional helpers, NOT a recurring weekly commitment. For teens needing 100+ sustained hours for college apps, pair FareStart with an anchor org (hospital JV, library teen council) rather than expecting depth-of-impact here. Conversely it's an ideal LOW-COMMITMENT first-time service experience for kids unsure they want a yearlong commitment, or for racking up incremental hours during senior-year crunch.

items.sourceName: Seattle Humane — Humane Teen Club & High School Service Shifts
items.insight: Seattle Humane runs a SEPARATE parent mailing list that gets PRIORITY UPDATES + EARLY REGISTRATION NOTICES before each public registration window opens — sign up at seattlehumane.org/get-involved/youth-school-programs (scroll to 'Stay informed' form). This is the single biggest overlooked Seattle volunteer hack: Summer Camp 2026 ($695/week, M-Th 8:30am-3:30pm, both Kids Day Camp and Teen Day Camp tracks) and Spring Break Workshops fill via this priority list FIRST, public registration second. Joining the list before the public announcement is the difference between getting in and being waitlisted.

items.sourceName: Seattle Humane — Humane Teen Club & High School Service Shifts
items.insight: Two unpublicized FAST-TRACK service-hour paths beyond the year-long Humane Teen Club: (1) Teen Spring Break Workshops earn THREE hours of community service in a single one-off workshop session (animal-themed lesson + behind-the-scenes shelter tour + furry-friend interaction); (2) 'Earn Service Hours at Home' lets teens log hours by donating, fundraising, or supporting Oogie's Ohana Pet Food Bank without ever entering the Bellevue shelter. Useful for teens who need quick documented hours for HS graduation requirements, or who can't commit to the recurring every-other-Saturday Teen Club schedule. Direct intake line for youth programs is (425) 373-5385 option 2 — separate from the main Seattle Humane line.

items.sourceName: Seattle Humane — Humane Teen Club & High School Service Shifts
items.insight: Equity hack for low-income family schools: Seattle Humane is now actively sponsoring FREE humane-education programming for Title 1 schools — teachers at qualifying schools can email EducationServices@seattlehumane.org to bring a humane educator to the classroom or schedule a sponsored field trip at zero cost. Most other youth animal-welfare programs charge for school visits. Worth flagging for school counselors at Title 1 schools across King County who may not realize the option exists.

items.sourceName: KCLS Teen Volunteer Program (TVP) & Teen Advisory Boards
items.insight: TVP was BORN remote (founded June 2020 over Zoom during pandemic library closures) and remains virtual-first by design — teens countywide can join WITHOUT being tied to a specific branch. This matters most for teens in more remote KCLS service areas (Maple Valley, Snoqualmie, Vashon Island, Skykomish, Carnation) who can't reliably get to a branch on weekday afternoons. Teen Advisory Boards are still branch-anchored (need to physically attend meetings at one specific library), but TVP itself has no geographic gating within King County. Direct librarian contact for TVP applications: Rochelle Brown, rochellb@kcls.org.

items.sourceName: KCLS Teen Volunteer Program (TVP) & Teen Advisory Boards
items.insight: TVP teens DESIGN and co-produce the workshops other teens attend — examples from prior cohorts include 'College Essays that Work', 'College Scholarships: Secrets to Success', a STEM Career Panel, 'Engineering Around the House: Paper Bridge Challenge', and a 'Teen Creative Society' arts series. This means a TVP teen can stack hours TWO ways simultaneously: hours for designing/leading a workshop AS organizer, PLUS hours for attending peer-led TVP workshops as participant. Most volunteer programs don't permit this dual-counting. Internal TVP-only workshops also exist on Resumes, LinkedIn, and Communication Skills — bonus pre-college soft-skill training built into the role.

items.sourceName: Seattle Children's Hospital Junior Volunteer
items.insight: Applications open THREE TIMES per year — March, July, AND November — not just spring as commonly assumed. But each cycle locks the volunteer into a fixed 6-month commitment window: March cycle = April-Nov, July cycle = Aug-Mar, November cycle = Jan-Aug. The next opening is noon PT Thursday July 16, 2026 (currently CLOSED). Apply in the cycle whose service window matches your teen's actual availability — if a March applicant can't honor April-Nov they'll be deferred. Free on-site parking is included once placed.

items.sourceName: Seattle Children's Hospital Junior Volunteer
items.insight: Three commonly assumed-but-FALSE expectations to verify before your teen applies: (1) NO summer-only volunteering — the FAQ explicitly says 'Not at this time' to summer-only availability, so don't pitch this as a summer-break activity; (2) NO baby cuddling positions; (3) NO medical shadowing — that's a separate Medical Observership program at /healthcare-professionals/education/medical-observations-job-shadowing/. Practical: nearly all shifts are weekdays Mon-Fri, starting between 9am and 2pm — teens with school-year afternoon sports/jobs will struggle to find a workable shift. Most placements are at the main 4800 Sand Point Way NE hospital; limited slots also at North Clinic (Everett), South Clinic (Federal Way), and Bellevue Clinic & Surgery Center.

items.sourceName: Northwest Harvest Volunteer
items.insight: Wayfinder's 'Kent SODO warehouse' description is dated. The Seattle-area distribution warehouse is now in AUBURN (2820 B St NW, Suite 109), and accepts only 4 volunteers per week, Mondays 10am-noon ONLY (weekend shifts on hold) — books out fast. For more capacity, drive to YAKIMA (Tue/Wed/Thu 10am-12pm AND 1-3pm + Fri 10am-12pm) or sign up separately for the SODO Community Market (a different retail-grocery operation, max 2 shifts/week on different days, no drop-ins). Spokane warehouse is currently on hold for individual volunteers, group inquiries only.

items.sourceName: Northwest Harvest Volunteer
items.insight: Minimum age is 9 (3rd grade), not 10 as currently listed in Wayfinder. Ages 9-15 require a parent or guardian to volunteer alongside; 16-17 can volunteer solo with a parental permission form on file. Hard logistics rules at every location: closed-toe shoes mandatory year-round (warehouse setting, expect to get dirty), max 40 people per shift (counted with supervisors for groups), no drop-ins (must schedule 24+ hours in advance), and the Auburn warehouse lacks an accessible restroom. Court-ordered community service hours: case-by-case only, not guaranteed. Application-to-first-shift turnaround is ~10 business days.

items.sourceName: Woodland Park Zoo Junior Zookeeper / Teen Volunteer
items.insight: The program rebranded to 'Teen Ambassador Volunteer Program (TAVP)' — 'Junior Zookeeper' and 'ZooCorps' (still listed in Wayfinder description) no longer exist as distinct programs. Only 15 teens accepted per cohort. 2026 applications CLOSED Friday March 27 at 5pm PST (interviews mid-April, decisions early May), so the next window for HS-only applicants is March 2027. Eligibility: rising 10th-12th graders entering Fall of the program year — current 9th graders are excluded. Stipend is a flat $300 for the summer (intended to cover transit, lunches, closed-toe shoes), NOT the variable 'paid stipend' currently described.

items.sourceName: Woodland Park Zoo Junior Zookeeper / Teen Volunteer
items.insight: Buried in the program calendar: in addition to the 20-hour minimum of self-scheduled volunteer shifts (June 29 – Sept 6), accepted teens MUST attend (1) an all-day orientation Friday June 26 8:30am-4:30pm and (2) at least 7 of 10 weekly cohort meetings, all on Wednesdays 3:30-6:30pm (Jul 1 through Aug 26, with a final celebration Sept 2 8:30-11:30am). Teens with conflicting Wed-evening commitments (sports practice, after-school jobs, music lessons) cannot complete the program — vet the Wednesday calendar before applying. Major accessibility win not advertised in summary copy: Canopy Neurodiversity Foundation (CNF) partners with WPZ to provide application + interview + ongoing coaching support specifically for ADHD and autism-identifying teens. Contact teenambassadors@zoo.org for CNF support before applying.

items.sourceName: Mary's Place (Family Shelters, WA)
items.insight: Mary's Place runs a structured high-school youth track called the Youth Action Program (YAP) — but it is INVISIBLE from the public /get-involved/volunteer landing page. That page only surfaces 'Volunteer Login' + 'New Volunteer Application' + a corporate-groups CTA; nothing names YAP. Parents only find YAP by stumbling onto blog posts (e.g. /blog/tag/youth+action+program). Real path for high-schoolers in Seattle: email volunteer@marysplaceseattle.org and ask specifically about YAP, OR follow the youth-action-program blog tag for the next cohort announcement, rather than filling out the generic 'New Volunteer Application' which routes to adult/corporate placements.

items.sourceName: Mary's Place (Family Shelters, WA)
items.insight: YAP volunteers commit to a recurring weekly slot (e.g. every Wednesday afternoon) at the Allen Family Center — located just off the Mt. Baker light rail station — supporting donation-room organization and staff. The program ALSO includes a structured book club (current cycle is reading 'Homelessness is a Housing Problem' by Gregg Colburn & Clayton Aldern). For college applications, this is the rare placement that pairs sustained hands-on service with a peer-discussion / advocacy-literacy component — counts as both 'service' and 'intellectual engagement', distinct from one-off donation drives.

items.sourceName: Seattle Aquarium Youth Ocean Advocates (YOA)
items.insight: YOA is THREE separate programs, not one — parents and students routinely conflate them. (1) TIDES = lowest barrier; any high-schooler joins via interest form; receives monthly newsletter + monthly digital meetups + quarterly Seattle-area events; minimal college-app weight. (2) CURRENTS = the actual hands-on Aquarium volunteer track (interpret to the public, behind-the-scenes trainings, field activities); selective application + interview + 5 mandatory training dates (~20 hours). (3) BREAKERS = invitation-only project teams reserved for experienced Currents who've already proven themselves; this is the strongest college-app credential because it pairs students with conservation professionals on intensive focused projects. Strategy: aim for Currents in 9th/10th grade, then earn a Breakers slot for 11th/12th — don't waste a senior-year app slot on Tides.

items.sourceName: Seattle Aquarium Youth Ocean Advocates (YOA)
items.insight: DEADLINE TRAP: as of late April 2026, the Summer 2026 YOA Currents interest form is ALREADY CLOSED — the window was January (interest opens) → March (mandatory online infosession) → April (application + decisions). The next entry point is the SCHOOL-YEAR session: interest form opens MAY 2026 (this month or next), September infosessions, October application + interview, November trainings, January 2027 first shifts. Action item for parents: bookmark the YOA page TODAY and check weekly in May. The infosession is mandatory before you can even receive the application — missing it kills the cycle. Email YOA@seattleaquarium.org to request notification when the form opens.

items.sourceName: Tacoma Rescue Mission Volunteer (Kitchen, Mentoring, High Impact)
items.insight: TRM has a separate 'High Impact Volunteer' tier most parents miss because the standard volunteerhub.com signup never mentions it. High Impact roles (Mentoring clients, Tutoring Youth or Adults, assisting Case Workers, Search & Rescue, front-desk shift) require an interview AND a 6-month minimum commitment — application is at trm.org/highimpact, NOT through the regular Volunteer Hub calendar. THIS is the college-app-grade tier for sustained-service narrative; kitchen shifts (3-hour blocks at 6-9am / 11am-2pm / 3-6pm) are valuable but read as drop-in service. For seniors building a 'depth over breadth' story, apply to High Impact as soon as 9th/10th grade.

items.sourceName: Tacoma Rescue Mission Volunteer (Kitchen, Mentoring, High Impact)
items.insight: AGE-FLOOR + LOGISTICS GOTCHAS at TRM that ambush families day-of: (1) Min age is 8 with adult, but Donation Center + Litter Pick Up are HARD 18+ regardless of waiver (safety rule, not guidance) — a 14-year-old waiver-holder will be turned away at the door for these two roles. (2) ALL minors require a completed Youth Waiver on file BEFORE the shift, not at check-in. (3) Account approval through rescue-mission.volunteerhub.com takes up to 5 business days — don't sign up for next-Saturday's shift on Wednesday and assume it will go through. (4) Dress code is enforced: closed-toed shoes + long pants required (no shorts, no sandals); they provide hairnets/gloves/aprons for kitchen but not the basic clothing. (5) On-site parking is genuinely limited — they explicitly encourage carpooling, plan accordingly.

items.sourceName: Habitat for Humanity (Build Sites + ReStore)
items.insight: Habitat's Youth Programs span ages 5–40 — there are structured tracks for every age, not just teens. Most parents miss this. Campus chapters can be founded at HIGH SCHOOL or college level (student-initiated; partner with the local affiliate). Starting/leading a Habitat Campus Chapter is a high-leverage college-app leadership pathway distinct from showing up to occasional build days — the chapter handles its own fundraising, awareness events, and build coordination.

items.sourceName: Habitat for Humanity (Build Sites + ReStore)
items.insight: The 16+ build-site rule and 14+ ReStore rule are HABITAT INTERNATIONAL guidance, not a hard floor — every one of the 1,400+ US affiliates sets its own actual age policy, insurance carrier, and waiver requirements. Always call your local affiliate before driving to a build day; ages and supervision rules can vary by 2+ years between adjacent affiliates (e.g., one county may allow 14-year-olds with a parent on supervised tasks while the next county over requires 18+). Find your local affiliate at habitat.org/volunteer/near-you.

items.sourceName: Habitat for Humanity (Build Sites + ReStore)
items.insight: Collegiate Challenge is Habitat's alternative-school-break pathway for college students (year-round, week-long service builds across the US). HS students can preview by joining a parent's affiliate or a faith/community group's local build, then frame service as a multi-year arc on the Common App — 'started building locally in 9th grade with my church group → led campus chapter as senior → committed to Collegiate Challenge in college.' This kind of cumulative through-line beats one-off heavy-hour weeks for showing real depth.

items.sourceName: International Rescue Committee (IRC) Youth Volunteer
items.insight: IRC's volunteer portal at rescue.org/volunteer (NOT the /take-action page in our DB) lists ~69 LIVE openings searchable by US city and role. Many are HS-relevant: Sacramento REP Youth Mentoring (after-school for HS-age refugees, available through Aug 30, 2026), Wichita ReConnect (mentor refugee youth ages 15–24 in social/civic/educational/career activities, through Jul 31, 2026), Oakland Youth Program Tutor (virtual or in-person homework help for refugee/immigrant K-12 students, ongoing). Real 'Available until' dates surface real openings — not a generic interest form.

items.sourceName: International Rescue Committee (IRC) Youth Volunteer
items.insight: Application process has an unusual cost step most parents don't expect: search → apply → orientation → IRC staff INTERVIEW → DONATE TO BACKGROUND CHECK FUND → complete background check. The donation funds the BG check itself (~$25–50 typical). Plan for that line item or ask the local office about hardship waivers up front — staff don't always volunteer that waivers exist unless you ask. Budget roughly 4–6 weeks from initial application to first volunteer shift, longer if multiple waitlists.

items.sourceName: International Rescue Committee (IRC) Youth Volunteer
items.insight: Most public-facing IRC roles (esp. tutoring, mentoring, ESL conversation partners) are listed only at the city level — Sacramento, Atlanta, Phoenix, Seattle, San Diego, Tucson, Wichita etc. There is NO national 'IRC volunteer' track; you have to pick the office closest to you and apply through THAT city's listings. If your nearest IRC office is far away, the Oakland Youth Program Tutor role explicitly accepts virtual volunteers — that's the only way to volunteer with IRC if you're not in one of their 28 US cities.

items.sourceName: Seattle Humane — Humane Teen Club & High School Service Shifts
items.insight: Three concurrent youth tracks — Humane Teen Club (school-year, ages 13–17, structured curriculum that PREPARES kids for future volunteer roles), High School Service Shifts (rising 9th–12th graders, drop-in service hours doing essential shelter tasks), and Teen Spring Break Workshops (3 hours of community service per workshop). The Teen Club is the feeder pipeline — kids who do HTC get priority for paid/structured volunteer roles in subsequent years, so starting in 8th–9th grade with HTC is the high-leverage long-game.

items.sourceName: Seattle Humane — Humane Teen Club & High School Service Shifts
items.insight: 'Earn Service Hours at Home' is an under-marketed track — kids can fundraise OR donate to Oogie's Ohana Pet Food Bank at Seattle Humane and get community-service-hour documentation. Useful for kids whose schedules can't accommodate in-shelter shifts (sports seasons, transportation barriers, immunocompromised siblings). Combine with NHS or church food-drive obligations to double-count hours where allowed.

items.sourceName: Seattle Humane — Humane Teen Club & High School Service Shifts
items.insight: Phone intake works and is fastest: (425) 373-5385 option 2, M–F, gets you straight to the Education Services team. This is materially faster than the Volunteer email, particularly in late winter/early spring when summer Day Camp registration windows open. As of 2026 spring, registration was already open for Kids Day Camp + Teen Day Camp — call to confirm waitlist status before checking the website (popular Bellevue weeks fill in <2 weeks of opening).

items.label: Washington Trails Association — 48-hour signup cliff is hard, but email opens a back door
items.detail: WTA work parties are auto-removed from the public schedule 48 hours before start time, even if half-empty — there's no on-page "sign up anyway" button. Inside that window, email volunteer@wta.org directly: crew leaders can sometimes squeeze one more if tools and lunch counts permit. Outside the email path, you're locked out. Plan teen weekend trail days the Wednesday before, not the Friday of. (verified 2026-04-27)
items.sourceName: Washington Trails Association Volunteer Trail Work Parties

items.label: WTA — Free trailhead day pass + free annual Discover Pass at 5+ days/yr
items.detail: WTA hands every work-party volunteer a free Discover-Pass-equivalent day pass at the trailhead — that alone covers the $11.50 day-use parking fee and offsets gas. Volunteer 5+ days in a calendar year and you earn a free annual Discover Pass ($30 value). For a teen building service hours over a summer, that's roughly $50-$70 in family parking costs back in your pocket — never marketed up-front. (verified 2026-04-27)
items.sourceName: Washington Trails Association Volunteer Trail Work Parties

items.label: WTA — Dress code is enforced, not requested. Sneakers = sent home.
items.detail: Long pants and sturdy CLOSED-TOE shoes are mandatory at the trailhead — crew leaders WILL turn volunteers away in shorts, leggings, or athletic sneakers without sturdy soles. The slot you signed up for is just lost. For sawyer crews (the prestige track for repeat teen volunteers), fully LEATHER boots are required, not just any closed-toe — plus long loose-fit pants (not athletic tights) and side-shielded eye protection. Plan a $60-$80 boot purchase if a teen wants to advance to saw work. (verified 2026-04-27)
items.sourceName: Washington Trails Association Volunteer Trail Work Parties

items.label: Hopelink — 1-week background check is on the critical path; can't volunteer same week
items.detail: Every Hopelink volunteer 16+ must pass a Washington State Patrol background check BEFORE attending the required virtual New Volunteer Orientation. Processing takes up to a week, then orientation is invite-only on a fixed schedule. Net: you cannot decide on a Sunday to volunteer next Saturday. Apply 2-3 weeks before any service-hours deadline. (verified 2026-04-27)
items.sourceName: Hopelink Volunteer (Eastside / North & East King County)

items.label: Hopelink — Most shifts are M-Th business hours; only a handful work for high-schoolers in school
items.detail: Stated openly on the page: "Most of our volunteer opportunities occur Monday through Thursday during regular business hours." The teen-feasible exceptions are narrow — Wednesday evening Avondale Park dinners (group prep + serve a meal for ~50 residents), and Friday afternoon Kirkland Warehouse sorting. Otherwise, school-break weeks are when teens can sustain weekly hours. Plan summer + winter break service-hour blocks accordingly. (verified 2026-04-27)
items.sourceName: Hopelink Volunteer (Eastside / North & East King County)

items.label: Hopelink — Holiday-season group slots fill 4 MONTHS out; lock Q4 by July
items.detail: Hopelink books group volunteer slots up to 16 weeks (4 months) in advance — and explicitly flags Oct-Dec as "more popular times" that fill far ahead. NHS chapters, scout troops, youth groups, faith-community service teams targeting Thanksgiving/December service should email VolunteerWithUs@hopelink.org by mid-July at the latest. Group sizes are 5-15 (all members 16+). After September, expect 'no holiday-season availability' replies. (verified 2026-04-27)
items.sourceName: Hopelink Volunteer (Eastside / North & East King County)

items.label: Eastside Friends of Seniors — Drivers must be 21+; high-schoolers locked out of the most-needed role
items.detail: EFS's biggest unmet need is volunteer drivers (medical appointments, grocery, essential services), but the published age cutoff is 21+ for drivers — high schoolers are excluded from this track entirely. Non-driving roles open at 16. The under-promoted teen-friendly slot: 'Specialized Support' — web design, IT/tablet/phone troubleshooting for seniors, fundraising, admin tasks. STEM-track teens have a near-untapped pathway here that AOs read as both service AND skill-application. (verified 2026-04-27)
items.sourceName: Eastside Friends of Seniors Volunteer

items.label: EFS — Minimum 6-month commitment + 2-5 hrs/month: this is relationship volunteering, not one-off shifts
items.detail: EFS requires a minimum of 2-5 hours/month for AT LEAST 6 months — designed to build a sustained relationship with one senior, not service-hour drop-ins. One-off-shift seekers chasing quick NHS hours will be turned away or redirected. Upside for college apps: same senior across 6+ months reads as authentic depth on Common App's activity description, vs. a transactional 'pulled some weeds once' line. Pitch this to families looking for ESSAY-quality service, not hour-quantity service. (verified 2026-04-27)
items.sourceName: Eastside Friends of Seniors Volunteer

items.label: EFS — Companionship can be done OVER THE PHONE: a real path for non-driving teens & rural Eastside
items.detail: EFS lists companionship as in-person OR phone-based — which most parents miss because the page leads with transportation visuals. Phone companionship + remote IT/tech help means a 16-year-old without a license, a kid out in Snoqualmie Valley with no easy Bellevue/Redmond commute, or a teen with mobility limits can still build a 6-month relationship with a senior. Non-obvious workaround for the driver-21+ cliff. (verified 2026-04-27)
items.sourceName: Eastside Friends of Seniors Volunteer

items.label: Hospital Junior Volunteer (multi-site) — application windows are tight + sometimes one-day-only
items.detail: For 2026: Orlando VA accepts ALL applications on a single day (Wed Apr 15, 2026); Holy Name Medical Center opens at exactly 7:00 a.m. on Tue May 5, 2026; Texas Health Alliance window is Jan 13–Mar 2; Houston Methodist West runs Feb 1–27. Parents who treat this as a 'when does summer start' search miss the slot. Calendar the open day, not the program start.

items.label: Hospital Junior Volunteer (multi-site) — acceptance is followed by a 2nd hurdle (TB test + drug screen + immunizations)
items.detail: Once selected, Texas Health, University Health (San Antonio), Houston Methodist, Atrium Health, UPMC Children's, and Medical City McKinney all require a criminal background check, urine drug screen, TB skin test (some require 2 PPD readings or a QuantiFERON Gold blood test), immunization review, sometimes a flu shot. Hospitals cover the cost but the lead-time can push the actual start date 2–3 weeks past the acceptance letter — front-load this before summer.

items.label: American Red Cross — Summer Youth Corps is a structured 11-week cohort, not drop-in volunteering
items.detail: Distinct from the generic 'become a volunteer' page: Summer Youth Corps requires 11 shifts across 11 weeks (one shift/week), age 13+, parent/guardian consent, and the volunteer Connection intake. Separately, a school-based Red Cross Club is a leadership/scholarship pathway — the school files a Club Constitution with the regional chapter and registers all members through Volunteer Connection. Two different commitments; they stack but aren't substitutes.

items.label: Special Olympics Unified Champion Schools — National Banner Recognition is a formal multi-year credential, not a participation badge
items.detail: Schools that sustain 10 standards (Unified Sports + Inclusive Youth Leadership + Whole School Engagement) across consecutive years earn National Banner Recognition Status. A student who launches/leads their HS's Unified Champion Schools effort earns a uniquely named credential AOs recognize — meaningfully stronger than 'volunteered at Special Olympics events.' Each year requires re-submitting a Commitment to Inclusion form via the state chapter (e.g., Special Olympics Washington).

items.label: Ronald McDonald House — meal-program is the only teen entry point, and it requires an adult chaperone
items.detail: Most individual volunteer roles are 18+ (Boston Harbor, Fort Worth chapters). The meal program opens at age 16 but requires a 1:2 adult-to-teen ratio at the Seattle chapter and a 21+ adult team leader at Charlotte; Southwest Virginia requires under-18s to be parent/guardian-accompanied in the kitchen. Practical implication for parents: a teen can't 'just sign up' — at least one adult has to commit alongside. Plan the cohort, not just the teen.

items.label: Crisis Text Line — strict 18+ + US SSN, but offers a unique grad-school practicum-credit pathway at 24 universities
items.detail: Hard 18+ requirement plus US Social Security Number (for background check) excludes high schoolers entirely — for under-18 mental-health crisis volunteering, look at TeenLine, Trevor Project youth ambassadors, or local TeenLink instead. For college-bound students pursuing social work, the Student Learning Practicum partners with 24 grad schools (Columbia SSW, NYU Silver, Rutgers SSW, Loyola Chicago, Hawaii Pacific, U Denver psychology, etc.) — practicum hours count toward the MSW 200–600-hour graduation requirement, completed remotely. Worth flagging to a senior choosing schools.
